items.title: Closed versioned object envelope
items.statement: The receipt has a fixed schema identifier and rejects unknown top-level fields, so version identity and accidental top-level extension are structurally falsifiable.

items.title: Basic artifact integrity fields are constrained
items.statement: Each file must declare a lowercase 64-hex digest and a positive byte count. This is a useful structural precondition even though the schema cannot prove that either value matches bytes.

items.title: Four files do not guarantee one file per required role
items.statement: The array only requires at least four entries and each entry chooses an enum role. A receipt with four duplicate roles, duplicate names, or duplicate digests passes while omitting other semantically expected roles; neither per-role cardinality nor cross-entry uniqueness is encoded.
items.impact: Consumers can accept an incomplete or ambiguous packet and later select different artifacts for the same role.
items.builder_discretion: Specify required role cardinality and uniqueness keys, or explicitly state that duplicates and absent roles are valid.

items.title: Packet identity is non-canonical and unbound to files
items.statement: Both packet identifiers are arbitrary nonempty strings, and no rule binds either value to the source_packet_archive entry, its digest, or its artifact name. Two receipts can name the same bytes differently or claim the same packet identity for different bytes.
items.impact: Callers cannot establish stable packet identity, deduplicate intake, or detect identity substitution from schema validity.
items.builder_discretion: Define canonical packet identity and its derivation or binding to the archive artifact.

items.title: Finding priorities lack referential integrity
items.statement: The finding ID array is unique, but finding_priorities may be empty, omit IDs, or contain unrelated keys because no property-name or coverage relationship ties the object to finding_ids.
items.impact: Priority-driven consumers can silently drop findings or process phantom findings.
items.builder_discretion: Require exact key-set equality or define explicit missing and extra key semantics in a representation that can be validated.

items.title: Timestamp and repository provenance are untyped
items.statement: generated_at_utc and source_repo only require nonempty strings. Invalid dates, non-UTC values, mutable branch labels, local paths, or ambiguous repository aliases all pass.
items.impact: Ordering, staleness checks, reproducibility, and source authority decisions cannot rely on schema validation.
items.builder_discretion: Constrain the timestamp to a UTC date-time and define a canonical repository plus immutable revision representation.

items.title: Artifact names accept unsafe and nonportable input
items.statement: artifact_name accepts any nonempty string with no length, normalization, separator, traversal, control-character, case-folding, or basename constraint. A consumer that treats it as a path can be exposed to traversal or platform-dependent collisions.
items.impact: Extraction, display, lookup, and persistence may escape intended roots, collide, or render deceptive names.
items.builder_discretion: Declare whether this is an opaque label or a safe relative path and constrain or sanitize at the authoritative boundary.

items.title: Negative constraints are unenforceable prose
items.statement: The receipt requires at least one nonempty string but supplies no stable constraint ID, scope, authority, severity, lifecycle, acknowledgement, or conformance result. Duplicates and contradictory strings pass.
items.impact: Consumers cannot deterministically apply, reconcile, migrate, or test constraints.
items.builder_discretion: Define a structured constraint contract or explicitly bound these strings to non-authoritative annotations.

items.title: Concurrent intake has no idempotency or revision contract
items.statement: The receipt has packet strings but no receipt ID, generation number, immutable revision, compare-and-swap token, or duplicate-resolution rule. Concurrent workers can emit different valid receipts for the same logical packet with no schema-visible winner.
items.impact: Last-writer behavior, duplicate processing, and stale overwrite are left to callers and can diverge across implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Specify idempotency identity and conflict or revision semantics at the receipt boundary.

items.title: Partial acquisition and recovery states are unrepresentable
items.statement: All file fields are required, but PacketFile has no acquisition, verification, quarantine, error, retry, or recovery state. A missing, corrupt, or temporarily unavailable artifact can only make the receipt absent or force fabricated completion data.
items.impact: Interrupted intake cannot be resumed or diagnosed from the contract, and consumers cannot distinguish pending from permanently failed packets.
items.builder_discretion: Define lifecycle states and retry or rollback ownership, or explicitly state that receipts are created only after an external atomic verification transaction.

items.title: Declared digest is neither verified nor authenticated
items.statement: A syntactically valid SHA-256 string proves neither that bytes were fetched and hashed nor that the digest came from an authorized publisher. There is no verification result, verification time, signature, signer, trust root, or content-addressed packet binding.
items.impact: A malicious or faulty producer can submit internally well-formed but substituted artifacts and matching invented metadata.
items.builder_discretion: Separate claimed metadata from verified observations and define authenticity authority and executable byte-comparison or signature oracles.

items.title: Privacy and data lifecycle are unspecified
items.statement: received_packet, source_repo, artifact_name, and free-form constraints can carry local paths, repository credentials, user names, URLs, or other sensitive strings, but the contract defines no redaction, classification, retention, deletion, or access policy.
items.impact: Receipts may persist or expose sensitive provenance without a defined handling boundary.
items.builder_discretion: Constrain sensitive fields and define classification, redaction, retention, and deletion behavior for persisted receipts.

items.title: Receipt validity can mislead GUI and support surfaces
items.statement: The model contains metadata but no received, verified, incomplete, stale, superseded, quarantined, or failed status. A GUI can only infer success from object existence and may present declared digest and byte size as verified truth.
items.impact: Users and support personnel can be shown a completed or trusted packet when only syntactic metadata exists.
items.builder_discretion: Provide authoritative lifecycle and verification state with reason codes and timestamps suitable for faithful display and diagnostics.

items.title: Offline and network-loss semantics are absent
items.statement: The schema records neither artifact locator nor whether metadata and bytes came from cache, local receipt, or remote fetch. It cannot distinguish offline-unavailable content from missing or invalid content, nor record deferred verification.
items.impact: Offline consumers cannot make deterministic availability or retry decisions from the receipt.
items.builder_discretion: Define location and availability semantics, cache provenance, and pending verification behavior if network retrieval is part of this boundary.

items.title: Receipt collections and strings are unbounded
items.statement: files, finding_ids, supersedes, negative_constraints, arbitrary priority keys, and all free strings have no maxima. A valid receipt can consume unbounded parser, validation, storage, rendering, or support resources; byte_size itself also has no upper operational bound.
items.impact: Schema-valid input can cause denial of service or unusable GUI and diagnostic output.
items.builder_discretion: Set justified cardinality, length, byte-size, and aggregate receipt limits or define streaming and rejection behavior.

items.title: Human-facing strings lack localization and accessible semantic structure
items.statement: Artifact roles are stable tokens, but artifact names and negative constraints are unlocalized free text with no locale, message key, structured meaning, or safe display label. If surfaced, consumers must guess pronunciation, translation, truncation, directionality, and accessible description behavior.
items.impact: Different GUI consumers can expose inconsistent, untranslated, clipped, or assistive-technology-poor receipt information.
items.builder_discretion: Keep protocol tokens nonlocalized while defining localized presentation keys or structured semantics and accessible fallback behavior where fields are user-visible.

items.title: Version migration and supersession are underspecified
items.statement: The outer receipt is fixed at v1 and embeds a findings matrix fixed at v3, while supersedes is only an array of arbitrary strings. There is no migration path, supported-version negotiation, target identity kind, uniqueness, cycle prevention, ordering, or compatibility rule.
items.impact: Older and newer producers or consumers can disagree on whether a receipt is readable and what supersession changes.
items.builder_discretion: Define migration and compatibility policy and make supersession references typed, unique, acyclic, and authority-bound.

items.title: Supersession can imply destructive invalidation without lifecycle rules
items.statement: supersedes records references but says nothing about whether prior receipts become hidden, invalid, deleted, retained, restorable, or still authoritative. It also lacks the actor and permission allowed to supersede.
items.impact: A consumer may destructively discard still-needed evidence or accept unauthorized history replacement.
items.builder_discretion: Define supersession as non-destructive lineage or specify authorization, retention, rollback, and user-visible effects.

items.title: Cross-document seams have no equality or ownership constraints
items.statement: The embedded finding_matrix is independent of the findings_matrix PacketFile role, and the received_packet string is independent of the source_packet_archive role. The schema does not say which is authoritative or require their IDs, versions, names, hashes, or contents to agree.
items.impact: A structurally valid receipt can combine metadata and files from different packets or matrix versions, yielding split-brain consumers.
items.builder_discretion: Add explicit content bindings and authority precedence across embedded metadata and referenced artifacts.

items.title: Structural schema lacks semantic acceptance oracles and named consumers
items.statement: The contract constrains JSON shape, but it defines no caller or consumer obligations and no executable oracle for file existence, actual digest, actual byte size, archive membership, matrix-to-file equality, completeness, or negative-constraint enforcement.
items.impact: Implementations can all pass JSON Schema validation while disagreeing on the receipt's core meaning and acceptance threshold.
items.builder_discretion: Name producer and consumer responsibilities and define falsifiable end-to-end verification receipts or tests beyond structural validation.

dimension_assessments.summary: No producer or consumer obligations, authority precedence, or acceptance threshold are defined.
Duplicate roles, unbound identities, incomplete priorities, and absent lifecycle states permit semantically invalid but structurally valid receipts.
No idempotency, revision, conflict, or stale-write rule exists.
Partial acquisition, corrupt artifacts, deferred validation, and failure causes cannot be represented.
Retry, resume, quarantine release, supersession rollback, and restoration ownership are absent.
Constraint, supersession, repository, publisher, and verification authority are not identified or authenticated.
Potentially sensitive free-form provenance has no classification, redaction, retention, access, or deletion contract.
Names and free strings accept unsafe, ambiguous, and deceptive values; claimed hashes are unauthenticated.
No authoritative state distinguishes declared metadata from received, verified, failed, stale, or quarantined truth.
Availability, cache provenance, remote retrieval, deferred verification, and retry semantics are absent.
Collections, strings, priority keys, byte sizes, and total receipt size are not operationally bounded.
User-visible free text lacks structured meaning and accessible presentation fallback, while unbounded values can defeat usable rendering.
Free-form human-facing strings have no locale or message-key contract; stable protocol role tokens are the only partial nonlocalized structure.
Fixed schema versions coexist with untyped supersession and no negotiation, migration, or compatibility policy.
No validation status, validator version, reason code, verification time, correlation ID, or diagnostic lifecycle is present.
Supersession may be interpreted destructively without authorization, retention, restoration, or user-visible effect rules.
Embedded matrix metadata and file-role artifacts are not bound, and packet identity is not tied to archive content.
Closed objects, constants, uniqueness for finding IDs, digest syntax, and positive size are structurally testable, but semantic byte, identity, role, and coverage oracles are absent.
The largest uncovered trust assumption is that receipt producers are honest: no signer, trust root, or independently verified observation separates claims from facts.
